title: Free generation on the inverse image of a second section-ring chart
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $L$ an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module], $S$ its section ring [def-sc-invertible-section-ring], $d>0$, $s\in S_d$, $U\subseteq X$ open, and $s|_U$ a free generator [def-sc-local-free-generator]. Let $\rho:S_{(s)}\to\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_X)$ satisfy $\rho(a/s^m)(s^m)|_U=a|_U$ for every $m\geq0$ and $a\in S_{md}$. Let $q:U\to\operatorname{Spec}S_{(s)}$ induce $\rho$ under the canonical identifications [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme], and put $g=\iota_s\circ q$ [def-pc-proj]. For every $e>0$ and $t\in S_e$, let $W\subseteq X$ be the ambient image of $g^{-1}D_+(t)$. The restriction $t|_W$ is a free generator of $L^{\otimes e}|_W$. Equivalently, on every subopen $V\subseteq W$, multiplication by $t|_V$ is a bijection $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_X)\to\Gamma(V,L^{\otimes e})$. No numerator or quotient equation on the second chart is asserted.

source.place: Tags 01N8 (local quotient construction and comparison) and 01NK (different positive degrees)

proof.text: On a local basis z of L inside U, write s=b z^d and t=c z^e. The free-generator hypothesis on s says b is a unit. Substitute exponent e and the homogeneous numerator t^d in hρ (using d*e=e*d). Coefficients of section-ring products are products, so this identifies ρ(t^d/s^e) with c^d/b^e.

source.place: Tags 01N8 (local quotient construction and comparison) and 01NK (different positive degrees)

proof.text: The preimage of D_+(t) under the s-chart inclusion is the principal open of t^d/s^e (Mathlib Proj.awayι_preimage_basicOpen). The affine basic-open preimage formula and hq therefore identify its pullback with the unit locus of c^d/b^e. Since b is a unit and d>0, this equals the unit locus of c, even in rings with nilpotents.

source.place: Tags 01N8 (local quotient construction and comparison) and 01NK (different positive degrees)

proof.text: On that locus t is a unit multiple of the tensor power of the local basis, hence freely generates. The resulting multiplication maps and their inverses glue, because the multiplication map on each patch is induced by the same section t. This yields bijectivity on every subopen of W. If W is empty the section types are singletons.
